descriptionChirho: Physical or military pursuit of a person or group, the core Qal meaning of actively chasing after someone to catch or overtake them.
Hostile pursuit with intent to harm or oppress, especially of the righteous or innocent; distinguished by Arabic iḍṭahada (اضطهد) and Korean pipbak (핍박) and Hindi satānā (सताना).
Abstract pursuit of a goal, ideal, or course of action such as peace, righteousness, or good; distinguished by Korean ttareuda (따르다) and Arabic saʿā/tabiʿa in non-hostile contexts.
Intensive or sustained pursuit, the Piel intensification conveying persistent, determined chasing or following; Arabic mutatibbiʿ (مُتَتَبِّع) and Korean chugu (추구).
Passive voice indicating being the object of pursuit or persecution; Arabic nuṭāradu (نُطَارَدُ), Korean jjotkim (쫓김).
Causative stem indicating causing or enabling pursuit of a target.
Passive of the Piel stem, indicating being intensively or persistently pursued or driven; Arabic yuṭāradu (يُطَارَدُ), Swahili -fukuzwa (be driven away).
